title: Alternative Six-Round V63 Integrals for MISTY1
summary: A roughly 70-bit-time attack on full MISTY1 is known; it remains open whether alternative six-round integrals can remove Phase 2 and realize the conjectured 64-bit-time improvement.

formal_statement.body: For the attack on full MISTY1, determine whether additional six-round $V_{63}$ integral structures can be obtained by fixing bits other than the last seven. If such structures exist, determine whether their additional filtering in Phase 1 suffices to eliminate Phase 2, yielding an attack consisting only of Phase 1 with time complexity approximately $2^{64}$, dominated by data decryption.

scope.domain: Symmetric-key cryptanalysis of full MISTY1 using six-round integral structures.
parameters: six rounds: round span of the sought integral structures
V63: integral-structure class sought under alternative fixed-bit choices
last seven bits: fixed-bit choice that the proposed structures would replace
approximately two to the sixty-four: target attack time complexity
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish whether the additional V63 structures exist and whether their Phase 1 filtering eliminates Phase 2 to yield the proposed Phase-1-only attack.

citations.label: A 2^70 Attack on the Full MISTY1

progress.summary: The source presents reducing the attack's data complexity as a problem for further research and proposes additional six-round integrals as a possible direction. It explicitly conjectures that alternative V63 structures would enable enough Phase 1 filtering for a roughly 64-bit-time attack.
citation_labels: Achiya Bar-On et al., A 2^70 Attack on the Full MISTY1
